newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil court to rule on Band B cell phone tender.
newsitem.headline: Brazil court to rule on Band B cell phone tender.

text.p: Brazil's Supreme Federal Tribunal, the country's highest court, is scheduled to vote Wednesday on whether a multi-billion dollar cellular phone tender is unconstitutional and if it should go ahead or not.

The court decision will be closely watched by 12 international consortia that on April 7 plan to bid for the Band B cellar phone concessions which include some of Brazil's most potentially lucrative service areas.
Sergio Motta, Brazil's Communications Minister has said the government expects to raise between $5 billion and $6 billion from the Band B cellular phone concessions.

The Supreme Court must decide whether President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's government can go ahead with the Band B tender, even though legislators have not even begun working on a general telecommunications deregulation bill.
The bill, which will regulate how private investment will develop the country's telecom services, is not expected to be approved by Congress before early 1998.
Analysts said it was difficult to predict how the Supreme Court would rule on Wednesday.
They said the case against the cellular concessions was strong, but that it was unlikely the court would be prepared to derail the government's first major privatization in the telecom sector.
"I think the court will weigh the political implications of a ruling against the cellular phone tender," said Jacobo Valentino, an analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
If the court ruled against the government, damage should be measured in terms of how long the cellular concessions were postponed, analysts said.
A brief two- or three-month delay would be viewed as a nuisance, but would not threaten the government's privatization drive.
However, the Cardoso administration would suffer a serious blow if the court forced authorities to hold back on the Band B project until the general telecom bill was approved.
"That would mean the Band B tender would be delayed until next year and perhaps several of the consortia would choose to bow out," said Vera Rossi, a telecom analyst at ING Barings.
The Supreme Court was scheduled to decide on the cellular phone concession case when it meets at 1400 local/1700 gmt Wednesday afternoon.
